design_type: descriptive repeated cross-sectional panel of occupation-by-industry wage cells
estimand: employment-weighted difference in log real mean hourly wage between renewable and non-renewable generation industries for workers in the same detailed occupation and survey year (and its variation by generation source, occupational group, and year)
identification_strategy: no causal identification; descriptive adjustment by occupation x year fixed effects isolates within-occupation comparisons across generation industries; composition decomposition separates occupational mix from within-occupation pay differences
journal_method_bar: Energy Policy expects transparent, reproducible empirical analysis with clearly stated data limitations, robustness checks, and policy-relevant interpretation; descriptive designs are acceptable when claims are bounded.

hypothesis_model_coverage.coverage: raw vs within-occupation gap and decomposition

power_or_feasibility_assessment.rationale: Five annual OEWS files yield about 2,000 detailed occupation-industry cells with published wages across 7 analytic generation industries; roughly 150-200 occupations appear in multiple industries, giving within-occupation contrasts. Geothermal (4-8 cells per year) and biomass (12-14) are thin, so their source-specific estimates are feasibility-limited and will be reported with that caveat. Year-to-year trend precision is limited because OEWS pools three years of survey panels.

causal_gate.reason: Design uses occupation x year fixed effects; scholar-causal audited it and confirmed FE serve as descriptive adjustment only (open backdoor paths via worker sorting and region), so claim strength stays descriptive.

method_specialist_routing.method_orientation: observational quantitative panel of repeated occupation-by-industry cross-sections
method_specialist_routing.rationale: Standard quantitative regression and decomposition on published aggregate statistics; no computational, qualitative, or linguistic component.

assumptions: OEWS cell means are unbiased estimates of the employment-weighted mean wage for each occupation-industry-year (subject to reported relative standard errors)
Detailed SOC occupations (2018 SOC) and six-digit NAICS generation industries are defined consistently across May 2021-May 2025 releases

Within a detailed occupation, job content is comparable enough across generation industries that wage differences reflect pay-setting and unobserved worker/plant differences rather than different jobs under one title
CPI-U (May values) adequately converts nominal wages to constant 2025 dollars

x.name: renewable generation industry
x.operationalization: 1 for NAICS 221111 hydroelectric, 221114 solar, 221115 wind, 221116 geothermal, 221117 biomass; 0 for 221112 fossil fuel and 221113 nuclear; 221118 other excluded from main contrast

y.name: log real mean hourly wage
y.operationalization: natural log of OEWS H_MEAN converted to May 2025 dollars with CPI-U (CUUR0000SA0, May of each year)

moderators.occupational_group: five groups from SOC major codes

threats: Worker sorting on unmeasured skill within occupations across industries
Regional composition and cost-of-living differences across industries (unobserved in national cells)
Small, noisy cells in geothermal and biomass, and suppressed cells
Three-year pooled OEWS samples smooth and overlap year-to-year estimates
Job-title heterogeneity within detailed occupations (e.g., sales roles in solar)
robustness_plan: Unweighted estimates with equal cell weights
Inverse sampling-variance weights based on reported mean-wage relative standard errors
Restrict to occupations observed in both renewable and non-renewable industries in every year (balanced set)
Alternative categorization: nuclear excluded (renewable vs fossil only)
Alternative categorization: hydroelectric excluded from renewable group

measurement_strategy.weights_justification: OEWS cell estimates are already design-weighted by BLS; regressions weight cells by estimated employment so estimates represent workers, with unweighted and inverse-variance alternatives as robustness.

adjustment_set: detailed occupation x year fixed effects
